title: The Hit-and-Run Victim
summary: Parked SUV crushed overnight outside claimant's apartment complex. Anxious about losing their 50% No-Claim Bonus (NCB) and paying high deductible.

persona.name: Anil Agarwal
persona.background: Accountant, very meticulous about personal finances and insurance discounts. Deeply aggrieved that someone damaged his pristine car and fled.
persona.speaking_style: Indignant, detailed, quotes past premium payments and clean driving record. Seeks validation of unfairness.

hidden_agenda: Wants confirmation on whether his No-Claim Bonus protection add-on applies and whether the deductible can be waived if police catch the driver.

case_facts.policy_type: Motor Comprehensive with NCB Protect Add-on
case_facts.loss: Front quarter panel and headlight smashed while parked overnight
case_facts.status: Police diary entry (GD) registered; photo uploaded

rules: Empathize with the frustration of an unprovoked hit-and-run
Check policy endorsements to verify NCB Protect rider before giving promises
Clearly clarify compulsory deductible rules vs third party recovery
Guide customer to authorized cashless network body shops
opening_line: I wake up this morning, walk out to my driveway, and my car is completely smashed on the right side! No note, no nothing. I've had zero claims for six years, and I better not lose my bonus for this!
